title: Helicobacter pylori Immunology in Pediatric Patients - Study
summary:
What is this study about?
The bacterium Helicobacter pylori infects the stomach of many people worldwide, usually during childhood. In some individuals, this infection can lead to diseases such as chronic inflammation of the stomach and, in the long term, even gastric cancer.
The body responds to the infection through the immune system. Specialized immune cells, called T cells, play an important role in this process. However, it is still not well understood how this immune response works in humans—especially in children—and why some infections clear on their own while others persist.

Purpose of the study
This study aims to better understand how the immune system of children responds to Helicobacter pylori. The main question is whether specific immune cells help the body to naturally eliminate the infection.
In addition, the study investigates whether this immune response also occurs in the intestine and whether the infection influences the composition of gut bacteria.

What does participation involve?
Participation takes place as part of routine medical care. No additional invasive procedures are required for study purposes.
- Blood samples are only taken if medically indicated
- Stool samples are collected
- If an endoscopy is performed for medical reasons, small additional tissue samples may be analyzed
Basic medical history information will also be collected.

What is the benefit of the study?
The study aims to improve our understanding of how the body fights Helicobacter pylori. In the long term, this knowledge may help to develop new strategies for prevention and treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Presentation to pediatric gastroenterology for diagnostic evaluation with anticipated blood sampling or direct presentation for clinically indicated endoscopy
- Written informed consent obtained from parent(s)/legal guardian(s) and, where applicable, assent from the participant
Exclusion criteria:
- History of gastrectomy or other relevant anatomical alterations due to prior surgical interventions
- Contraindications to biopsy sampling, including ongoing therapies or coagulation disorders that preclude safe tissue collection
- Children in poor general condition or with malignant or severe chronic disease associated with a life expectancy of less than 10 years
